needs: bytes as text (&r [byte], int_of, slicing s[a..b])
loops over bytes with index cursors
a small struct (position record) or several return values from a parser
numeric parse of up to 9 digits
calling earlier units from later ones (valid -> compare -> comparator -> satisfies)
bytes.compare / manual byte compare for ASCII text order
pitfalls: prerelease starts at the FIRST '-' after the patch number; a '-' inside it is an identifier char (1.2.3-a-b)
build '+' may follow a prerelease, and a '-' after '+' belongs to build
all-digit identifier leading-zero rule applies to prerelease only, never to build (1.2.3+01 valid)
all-digit identifier vs non-digit: numeric is lower; numeric ids compare as numbers (2 < 11), text ids as ASCII (uppercase before lowercase)
shorter prerelease list is lower only when all shared ids are equal
bare version beats any prerelease of the same core
empty identifier checks: 1.2.3-, 1.2.3+, a..b, trailing dot
compare must return exactly -1/0/1 (bytes.compare may return other magnitudes)
'>=' and '<=' are two-byte operators; '>= 1.0.0' (space) is an Err
upper bound has no prerelease, so 2.0.0-rc.1 satisfies ^1.5.0; there is no special prerelease rule
range validation covers the whole range even after an earlier comparator failed; and the version is validated too
doubled, leading and trailing spaces and the empty range are Err; no panics on odd bytes (index bounds)
difficulty_notes: Pure byte-string parsing with no heap, so no buffer or ownership trouble; the difficulty is the many small rules (validity, identifier ordering, range desugaring) and getting ~490 oracle cases exactly right, especially the 400-case compare/satisfies grids. Satisfies has 300 of 492 cases, so desugaring errors (caret/tilde bounds, prerelease edge at the upper bound) cost the most. The plan's helper units (ident_list_ok, pre_compare, comparator_holds) are not graded by the audit; only the three public functions are, in the pinned shapes. Reference passes 492/492; the oracle was cross-checked against an independent implementation (0 diffs) and hand-computed brief examples.
